flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e4 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: I know e4 fights for the center. If this sentence is the whole opening curriculum, every pawn push will sound identical. Tell me it opens lines for the queen and bishop, or just stop calling a 20-centipawn book move 'the strongest' like I solved a puzzle.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: This is ply 1 with the square swapped. Same verdict, same because, same quip. I am not learning a dialogue; I am hearing a stamp.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f4 puts it at risk of attack from the black pawn. A better move would have been moving your g1-knight to f3.
flags.critique: This is the King's Gambit. I offered a pawn on purpose. You tagged it hanging and lectured me like I left a piece en prise. Nf3 is a quieter way to play, fine, but calling f4 a piece-safety accident is the opposite of teaching the opening I just played.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on f4 with your e-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: I accepted a gambit, I did not find a blunder. 'Undefended' is the entire point of 2.f4. Teach that I am a pawn up and White wants development and the f-file, not that I sniped a loose pawn.

flags.quote: Moving your g1-knight to f3 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: The reason you play Nf3 in the King's Gambit Accepted is to stop ...Qh4+. That is the first tactic every club player is told. 'Central squares' could be pasted onto any developing move. You missed the only lesson this ply exists to teach.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: This is the Fischer Defense: ...d6 so I can hold the gambit pawn with ...g5 and not get wrecked by a knight landing on e5. Another center-control stamp. Two plies after accepting the pawn, you still have not mentioned that I am trying to keep it.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 is a mistake, but moving your b1-knight to c3 would be better.
flags.critique: Why? You spent 191 centipawns and gave me a name and a better move with zero idea. e5 opens the d-file, gives up the d4 pawn's support, and lets Black recapture into a queen x-ray. Nc3 develops and keeps the center intact. That sentence is a verdict with the lesson stripped out. The only tagged reason is saves_piece, which does not even describe what e5 did.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your d-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and it unveils an attack from your queen on the black queen.
flags.critique: The e5 pawn is defended by the knight on f6. This is a recapture, not winning an undefended pawn. The queen x-ray on the open d-file is the real sentence — keep that, delete 'undefended' and the wins_material tag before I stop believing you when a piece is actually hanging.

flags.quote: A better move would have been taking the queen on d1 with your queen because you fork the white f3-knight and the white c1-bishop and you skewer the white king, exposing the white f1-bishop.
flags.critique: The queens are staring at each other on the open d-file. ...Qxd1+ trades queens with check and forces Kxd1, so White loses castling. Your queen is recaptured immediately; she does not keep a fork on f3 and c1 or a skewer through the king onto f1. That is tactic-detector word salad. You also led with the f4 pawn still hanging, which is real but secondary to missing the queen trade.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c4 is a mistake, but moving your f1-bishop to b5 would be better.
flags.critique: Empty again, and you tagged no reasons at all on a 175-centipawn swing. Bb5 pins the knight on c6 and fights for the center with a piece. c4 is a pawn lunge that does not develop. If you cannot say why the alternative is better, do not bother naming it.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to c5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No because-clause. The bishop comes out attacking toward f2 after White wasted a move on c4. Development is true and useless. Tell me the bishop is aiming at the uncastled king, or admit you had nothing.

flags.quote: A better move would have been moving your b1-knight to c3 because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: The first sentence actually taught me: e5 is hanging to both knights. Then the improvement is Nc3 'because center,' which is the same stamp as ply 1. If Nc3 develops and keeps e5, say that. Do not bait-and-switch a hanging-pawn lesson into fog.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f6 is playable, but moving your c5-bishop to e7 would be better.
flags.critique: ...f6 kicks the bishop and also rips my king open. ...Be7 challenges g5 without shoving the f-pawn. You tagged saves_piece and king_safer and then explained neither. I needed 'this weakens your king' or 'Be7 asks the bishop to trade without creating holes.'

flags.quote: Moving your g5-bishop to h6 is the strongest move because it saves your h6-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop is not on h6 until I put it there. You named the destination and then congratulated me for saving the piece that now lives on that square. It was hanging on g5 after ...gxf6. Say that.

flags.quote: Moving your c6-knight to e5 is a mistake, but moving your queen to e7 would be better because it attacks the king directly.
flags.critique: 'Attacks the king directly' is just 'check' in a costume. Why is the knight jump the mistake — does it hang, does it let White take over e5, does it miss a forcing check? Qe7+ is a check on the uncastled king. Put that in English and tell me what ...Nce5 failed to do.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e5 with your f-pawn is a blunder because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: That sentence is backwards. Taking an undefended knight would be the reason the capture is good, not why it is a 766-centipawn blunder. The f-pawn left and Qh5+ rips my king open — that is the lesson. Recapturing with the knight keeps the shield and opens the d-file. You praised the grab and buried the king hunt.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to h5 is the strongest move because it puts the opponent in check.
flags.critique: I can see the plus sign. The lesson is that ...fxe5 opened the h5–e8 diagonal and the queen check forces the king into the open. 'Because check' teaches nothing about the punishment I just walked into.

flags.quote: Moving your king to e7 is the strongest move because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: The king is running from Qh4-shaped check onto the exact diagonal where Bg5+ will skewer it against the queen. You tagged both king_more_exposed and king_safer, then picked the lie. This is a desperate flight, not a safety improvement, and 'That's the one' on it is insulting.

flags.quote: A better move would have been moving your knight to f6 because it gives your pieces more room to move.
flags.critique: You already knew the queen was hanging to the g5-bishop — that half is fine. Nf6 is not 'room to move.' It lands on the skewer ray (g5–f6–e7–d8) and blocks the bishop from the queen. I stepped the king off the line and left the queen to die. Teach interposition, not mobility.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d8 with your g5-bishop is the strongest move because you come out a rook ahead and it unveils an attack from your queen on the black pawn.
flags.critique: I took a queen. If the king recaptures the bishop, SEE nets something like a rook in your buckets, but I am not 'a rook ahead' in any human sense — I won the queen the skewer was built for. The extra discovered attack on a pawn is noise. Say you win the queen.

suggestions.title: Do not explain bad captures as benefits
suggestions.detail: select-insight sets explainPlayedAsBenefit for concept `capture` even when classification is mistake/blunder, so ply 24 becomes 'blunder because the knight was undefended.' A 1200 hears that taking a piece is why they blundered. Gate: if classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, never use pickBenefitReasons for the played because-clause. Prefer king_safety / pawn_shield / refutation punchline. Also stop letting `capture` outrank `king_safety` in CONCEPT_PRIORITY unless kingMoreExposed and pawnShieldDamage are false.

suggestions.title: Drop forks that die on the recapture
suggestions.detail: ...Qxd1+ is a queen trade with check. verifyLikelyTactics still emits fork (Nf3, Bc1) and skewer (king, Bf1) from a queen that is recaptured on d1. A 1200 cannot parse that word salad and misses the real idea: trade queens, force Kxd1, White cannot castle. If SEE shows the capturing piece dies next, keep check / wins_material / forces king recapture, drop fork/skewer/discovered on the dead piece.

suggestions.title: Teach exposed-king checks, not 'because check'
suggestions.detail: Qh5+ after ...fxe5 is the whole game, and the bank line is 'it puts the opponent in check' / 'attacks the king directly' (also ply 22). Rank pawn_shield and king_more_exposed above bare `check` when the check is the refutation of a shield wreck, and describe the open diagonal or the flight square. Forced king flights (ply 26) must not emit king_safer; if king_more_exposed is also present, drop king_safer.

suggestions.title: Name the hanging square, not the destination
suggestions.detail: saves_piece uses ownedPhrase on the piece after the move, so Bh6 'saves your h6-bishop from capture.' A 1200 rolls their eyes. Pass the from-square (or the hanging origin) into move-copy so it reads 'saves your bishop on g5' / 'saves your bishop from capture on g5.'

suggestions.title: Frame opening pawn offers as gambits
suggestions.detail: 2.f4 tagged hanging and piece_safety, then Nf3 and ...d6 got center_control. Club players know the King's Gambit and Fischer's ...d6/...g5 idea. Add an `offers_pawn` (or opening-phase gate on hanging for a just-pushed pawn with inaccuracy-sized loss) and a `prevents_check` fact: after Nf3, ...Qh4+ is no longer a check. Use that instead of hanging/center on plies 3–6.

suggestions.title: Never name a better move with no because
suggestions.detail: Ply 9 (e5 → Nc3) and ply 15 (c4 → Bb5) are 'X is a mistake, but Y would be better' with empty or junk reasons. missedImprovementSentence should refuse to emit a suggestion unless suggestedBecause is non-null, and discourse should always contrast at least one suggested benefit (development, pin, center pawn kept) against a problem reason. A 1200 already knows they erred; they opened the coach to learn why.

suggestions.title: Call a block a block
suggestions.detail: Nf6 vs Kd6 is interposing on the g5–d8 skewer, not mobility ('gives your pieces more room to move'). When the suggested to-square lies on a skewer/check ray between attacker and target, emit a `blocks_line` (or reuse pin/skewer with an interpose slot) instead of mobility/development. Same pattern will fire on any 'step off the line and drop the back piece' king run.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures undefended
suggestions.detail: wins_material copy uses 'the N was undefended' when SEE >= pieceValue-50. That fired on dxe5 (pawn defended by Nf6) and helped the ply-24 polarity bug. Require zero legal defenders of the captured unit, not merely a high SEE net. For Bxd8, if SEE nets ~600 after Kxd8, say you win the queen (or queen for bishop) instead of materialLabel's 'a rook' bucket.

whatWorked: Ply 7 d4: unveiling Bc1 onto the f4 pawn is a real discovered-attack lesson, not center fog.
Ply 8 ...Nf6 → play ...g5 to hold the gambit pawn: the Fischer idea, even unnamed.
Ply 10 ...dxe5: queen discovery down the newly opened d-file onto d4.
Ply 17 Bg5 problem clause: e5 hanging to both knights is concrete and true.
Ply 19 exf6: taking the pawn that was attacking the g5-bishop.
Ply 20 ...gxf6: removing the defender of Bg5.
Ply 27 Bg5+: actually names the king-and-queen skewer on the long diagonal.
